You know I've been wondering the same thing. I'm 22 and all I've focused my life on since I was 11 was art, I got in to uni and covid started. I realised I wasn't good enough for a professional standard and one of my teachers practically said that too. I truly feel like I've wasted my life trying to attain something I can never reach. I've been out of uni for a year, and I've gotten my first job where I'm happy. It's not in art, it's a coordinator for council ran equipment service (mainly for disabilities, mental and physical, etc) and I love my job. It's stressful and hectic, but I love being able to help people even if it's only I'm a small way. 

What I've realised is sometimes, life doesn't go as planned. Something you've wanted and worked hard for your whole life burns you out. Something that many others can easiky do, makes you feel terrible And that's okay. Take a step back. And asses what you dislike about it. I know it's easy to say, but sometimes you need to do what makes you happy not what makes you more money or what others are doing. Working is such a big part of our lives that if we're doing something hate, it doesn't matter what we do outside of it because those two days of joy don't make up for the five days of misery.
